analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 2222-3171). The change is documentation and test-procedure only; no executable code, authorization logic, attestation, encryption or billing paths are modified in these excerpts. Security-relevant statements I checked:
- Test fixtures use temporary directories, in-memory KEKs and ephemeral cache keys. Persistent-key phases require an isolated namespace. CLICommandSandbox and service/fan tests must use injected boundaries and never touch real sudo, launchd, Keychain or production endpoints (lines ~2628-2635).
- SSD prefix cache test notes (lines 2278-2301, 2743-2790) describe tamperFailsClosed, which requires authenticationFailed on valid-but-altered metadata. They also describe the donation, ready-receipt and refusal tests. This is consistent with T-041's AAD authentication and fail-closed claims, and it does not change cache scoping, TTL, HMAC naming or disk-budget policy.
- Status canonical byte tests (lines 2662-2680) keep the Swift and Go golden vectors identical, which supports the TB-009 status-signature compatibility.
- The MiMo/native selected-evidence gates stay opt-in. The docs state that missing inputs must not be replaced by synthetic evidence and that production admission and reserve defaults must not be loosened.
- The benchmark and report tooling (radix, teacher-forced, attention replay) has no production serving authority.
No new attack surface, invalidated assumption or threat-model gap was identified. Later passes need only confirm that the referenced workflow, script and test changes elsewhere in the PR match these doc claims. I could not see them, so that is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
